_meta.purpose: The refs/heads/main ruleset for SOLE_OWNER mode. Identical to main-ruleset.json except for the two parameters that require a second human. Prepared by M29-I; NOT APPLIED.
_meta.which_ruleset_applies: Read .github/governance/ownership.json. mode SOLE_OWNER applies this file; mode MULTI_PERSON applies main-ruleset.json. Applying both, or the wrong one, is caught by verify_repository_governance.php.

differences_from_multi_person.required_approving_review_count: 1 -> 0. GitHub forbids approving your own pull request, so on a one-human repository any value above zero blocks every merge rather than causing a review. Zero is the honest setting; it is recorded as DEFERRED in ownership.json, not as satisfied.
differences_from_multi_person.require_code_owner_review: true -> false. Every rule in .github/CODEOWNERS is commented out and every owner is an unresolved placeholder. Requiring review from owners the file does not resolve either blocks everything or enforces nothing — the M29-A defect.
differences_from_multi_person.require_last_push_approval: true -> false. It invalidates an existing approval when new commits are pushed. With zero required approvals there is none to invalidate, so true would assert a protection that cannot operate.

what_is_NOT_relaxed: deletion — main still cannot be deleted
non_fast_forward — main still cannot be force-pushed
pull_request — a pull request is still required; direct pushes to main are refused
dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push — retained, so the setting is already correct if the mode later changes
required_status_checks — all seven contexts, strict, unchanged. These are the real teeth under SOLE_OWNER
_meta.note_on_bypass: bypass_actors is empty here for the same reason it is empty in main-ruleset.json. A sole owner with admin rights can already disable a ruleset deliberately and visibly; a standing bypass would let them merge past a failing financial gate with no trace at all. See BREAK_GLASS.md.
